title: refactor(types,plugin-kanban): retire ColumnWidthConfig / ColumnWidthConfigSchema (objectui#10582)
body:
Fixes #10582
Clause-②: yes

## What this does

Deletes `ColumnWidthConfig` (`packages/types/src/complex.ts`) and its Zod mirror `ColumnWidthConfigSchema` (`packages/types/src/zod/complex.zod.ts`), together with both `@object-ui/types` barrel exports (`src/index.ts`, `src/zod/index.zod.ts`) and the `@object-ui/plugin-kanban` re-exports (`src/types.ts`, `src/index.tsx`). This is ADR-0049 enforce-or-remove on a declaration that no key references and nothing reads. The governing direction is triage's written retire direction on the card (first grade, comment `5831964491`), not a maintainer ruling.

- The kanban retirement docblock in `complex.ts` no longer says the type survives. It now says `ColumnWidthConfig` lost its one reader to objectui#8522 and is deleted here, and it points at the pin.
- `zod-mirror-parity.test.ts`: the `complex.zod.ts#ColumnWidthConfigSchema` pair leaves `MIRRORS`, `Declared` and the two import lists. `EXPECTED_MIRROR_PAIRS` follows the registry down by one, which is what the census failure message instructs ("update EXPECTED_MIRROR_PAIRS ... and nothing else"). The header sentence that names the pair under objectui#7664 is history and stays as it is.
- New pin: `packages/types/src/__tests__/column-width-config-retired-10582.test.ts`.
- `.changeset/10582-retire-column-width-config.md`: `minor` for `@object-ui/types` and `@object-ui/plugin-kanban`, with the breaking semantics and a migration section. No `major`.

## Premise, re-measured on `origin/main` `5c61e5241` (in-repo evidence only)

- `git grep ColumnWidthConfig` over the whole tracked tree. Outside `.changeset/`, it hits only the declaration, the mirror, the four re-exports, docblocks and the parity ledger. Per directory, case-insensitive, with a lit control on the same instrument:
  - `content/`: 0 hits (control `KanbanSchema`: 19);
  - `examples/`: 0 hits (control `KanbanSchema`: 3);
  - `apps/`: 0 hits (control `@object-ui/types`: 32);
  - `skills/`: 0 hits (control `@object-ui/types`: 17). There is no governed row to split out.
- Shape level: `defaultWidth` appears only in the type and the mirror. No schema key references either name. The one key that did, the `'kanban'` arm's `columnWidths`, retired with that arm (objectui#8802).
- No reader, no producer and no doc that teaches building one were found, so the stop condition did not fire.
- **H2 measured:** `one-authority-per-exported-name-6273.test.ts` has no ledger row for the name. It has one historical comment inside the objectui#7664 narrative, and that comment stays true as history. The file is not edited.
- **H4, sharpened:** I read the published 17.6.0 tarballs from npm.
  - `@object-ui/plugin-kanban@17.6.0` exports `ColumnWidthConfig` from its entry. There it is the package's own declaration, and `KanbanSchema.columnWidths` is typed with it.
  - `@object-ui/types@17.6.0` exports neither name (lit control: `BaseSchema` appears in 42 files of the same tarball). The pair entered `@object-ui/types` in this unreleased window with objectui#7664, so for that package it leaves before any version publishes it. The changeset says so.
  - Consumers outside the repo cannot be measured from here.
- **H5, precedent followed:** objectui#7068's retirement of `ActionCallback` / `ActionCallbackSchema`. There, a standalone retired pair is DELETED rather than tombstoned, and its absence is pinned (`action-callback-retired-7068.test.ts`). A tombstone (`?: never` / `retirementTombstone()`) exists for a member key under `.passthrough()`. A standalone type has no such hatch: an importer gets TS2305, "has no exported member", which is the loud refusal. The objectui#8522 retirement of `useColumnWidths` (PR objectui#10549) was a plain deletion too. I found no tombstone-export convention for retired type names in this repo.

## The pin, and proof that it can fail

The pin has three readings, each with a lit control on the sibling `CardTemplate` / `CardTemplateSchema` that did not retire:

1. The `ColumnWidthConfigSchema` name is `in` neither `complex.zod.ts` nor the `@object-ui/types/zod` barrel, checked at runtime.
2. `complex.ts` declares no `ColumnWidthConfig`, and neither entry file (`index.ts`, `zod/index.zod.ts`) exports either name. Both are read off the AST, so the docblocks that tell the story do not count.
3. Tree-scoped: no TypeScript source under `packages/`, `apps/` or `examples/` declares or exports either name. A re-declaration in another package would type-check cleanly, and only this reading sees it.

Each mutation leg went through `ablation-replace.mjs`. Its anchor had to hit, the landing was proven by the blob hash, and the restore was proven by blob == HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD`. The pin imports relative `src` paths, not a package `exports` specifier, so no dist build sits between the mutation and the reading.

| leg | mutation | predicted | observed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A1 | re-plant `export const ColumnWidthConfigSchema` in `complex.zod.ts` | readings 1 and 3 red | 2 failed / 4 passed |
| A2 | re-declare `export interface ColumnWidthConfig` in `plugin-kanban/src/types.ts` | only reading 3 red | 1 failed / 5 passed; offender `packages/plugin-kanban/src/types.ts: ColumnWidthConfig` |
| A3 | re-add `ColumnWidthConfig` to the `index.ts` export list | readings 2 and 3 red | 2 failed / 4 passed |

The first A1 attempt was a null run. The replacement contained the anchor, so the tool refused because the anchor count could not drop. It restored the file and measured nothing. The leg was rerun with a disjoint anchor, and the table records that rerun.

**Reverse check on the consumer side:** the `@object-ui/types` dist was rebuilt, and its one `ColumnWidthConfig` hit is the docblock sentence. I re-planted `ColumnWidthConfig` in `plugin-kanban/src/types.ts`'s re-export list and ran `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-kanban type-check`. It went red with `error TS2305: Module '"@object-ui/types"' has no exported member 'ColumnWidthConfig'`, and the restore was proven. This shows the green type-check reads the rebuilt `.d.ts`, not a cached one.

The per-file counts are identical when the same command lints the base blob of each file through `--stdin`, and the new pin has none. The 1 error is the `no-restricted-imports` finding on the `FormField` re-export in `packages/types/src/index.ts`, and it is present on the base blob.

## Acceptance notes

- **Pending changesets that this retirement supersedes.** `check:changeset-claims` (report-only) asked for 35 pending bodies to be re-read. Four of them name the type:
  - The objectui#8522 entry says "`ColumnWidthConfig` stays exported from `@object-ui/types` and from this package." That was true of that change.
  - The two objectui#7664 entries list the pair among the declarations that moved into `@object-ui/types`.
  - The objectui#7742 entry carries a dated note saying the type has no reader.
  
  This PR's own entry states the supersession in the same release section, for both packages. It edits none of those four files, because they are outside the claimed file surface. If the seat prefers an in-body dated note on the objectui#8522 entry, following the precedent where objectui#8522 added one to objectui#7742, it is a one-paragraph, prose-only edit.
- **Shared ledger.** objectui#10608 may also delete rows from `zod-mirror-parity.test.ts` and move `EXPECTED_MIRROR_PAIRS`. Whichever PR lands second merges `main` (no rebase, no force-push) and takes the constant from the registry, as the census message says. PR objectui#10710 edits `packages/types/src/index.ts` in a separate hunk.
- **Spec Main Shape Gate: not applicable.** Neither deleted declaration is spec-derived: both are plain local declarations with no `@objectstack/spec` reference, so objectui's compile against objectstack `main` cannot move with this diff.
- **`check:readme-exports` not run.** No README names either symbol (whole-tree grep above), and the gate needs every package built.
- `check:test-path-roots` classifies the pin's four filesystem reads as "unknown", because they go through a parameter or a loop binding. Every one of them is rooted at the pin's own `import.meta.url`, which is the same shape as the `action-callback-retired-7068` walk.
